claims.text: The target material is a Ta-containing refractory high-entropy alloy, exemplified by Ta-Nb-Mo-W-V.
The target alloy has a BCC solid structure near its melting point.
Standard experimental measurements of the target alloy's melting properties are infeasible.
An MTP trained specifically on liquid configurations of Ta-based refractory HEAs can replace full ab initio thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method will estimate melting free energies within 2% of ab initio accuracy.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by two orders of magnitude.
Including high-temperature liquid snapshots in the training set prevents liquid-phase extrapolation or 'liquid structure collapse.'
Liquid-structure collapse is a common failure mode of standard EAM potentials.
The MTP training data should contain both solid- and liquid-phase configurations of the Ta-based alloy.
The potential should be used in a perturbative free-energy scheme to calculate the solid-liquid free-energy difference while avoiding extensive direct ab initio liquid sampling.
The solid-liquid coexistence region for the Ta-based system is approximately 2500-3500 K.
A simulation cell of at least 500 atoms is required to capture local lattice-distortion effects.
The relevant multicomponent liquid exhibits short-range order and local structural distortions.
Standard EAM potentials fail to capture the liquid structure because their functional forms do not represent the complex chemical environments of refractory multicomponent liquids.
An MTP can learn a nonlinear mapping from local atomic environments to energies and forces and thereby model the high-entropy liquid more accurately than EAM without DFT-level sampling cost.
The free-energy landscape is sufficiently smooth near melting that a perturbation scheme requires fewer sampling points than full thermodynamic integration.
The calculated melting temperature and latent heat will agree with ab initio reference values within statistical error.
Computational time per free-energy point will decrease from days with DFT to hours with the MLP, enabling high-throughput composition screening.
Insufficient liquid-phase training coverage can produce extrapolation error and an apparently stable but incorrect free-energy prediction.

A blind high-temperature liquid test against DFT molecular dynamics, including free-energy, RDF, latent-heat, and timing measurements, can distinguish genuine efficiency from training-set error or error cancellation.

contradictions.description: The main prediction is a two-orders-of-magnitude cost reduction, but the qualitative 'days to hours' statement does not necessarily imply 100x, and the falsification rule rejects only reductions below 10x. Thus a 10-99x reduction could fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
Accuracy is specified as within 2% in the hypothesis but only as within unspecified statistical error in the predicted outcome, leaving inconsistent operational accuracy criteria.
